annotations.title: Check several claims at once against published records

description: About to state several numbers, dates, limits or statuses in one answer? Send them here first, in a single call. Each claim is a few plain words naming what it is about plus the value you were going to state; for each one this reports whether a published record of ours carries that value, with the field it matched, how closely (exact, case-insensitive, normalised, same number, or inside a longer stored value), the source URL and the verbatim passage from that page. Use it to check a draft answer, a table you assembled, or figures another tool gave you. Verdicts per claim: confirmed, in_the_source_quote_only, no_match_in_the_records_searched, or not_routed. It never calls a claim false: this catalogue is finite, so a claim we hold no record of comes back as no_match with the datasets that were searched named beside it, and the best-matching record's own published values shown so you can see what we do say. For one claim when you already know the dataset, verify_quote is cheaper and takes a record id.

claims.description: The claims to check, 1 to 8. Each is routed separately and costs up to `datasets` register reads, so send the figures you actually intend to state.

claim.description: What the value is about, in plain words, including the thing itself — a state, chemical, product, version, certificate or standard number. e.g. "retainage cap on public work in Ohio", "Python 3.11 end of support". Common words are ignored; the rest route the claim.

value.description: The value you were going to state, as you would state it — "8%", "2027-10-31", "$832,750", "no longer supported".

datasets.description: How many of the best-matching registers to search per claim, 1 to 5. Default 2. More widens the chance of finding the record and also of an off-topic match; every register searched is named in the reply.
